title: Data systems & reporting
description: Give staff a map or dashboard backed by a reporting pipeline they can check against source records.
keywords: Data systems & reporting Return to top Working example Open demo Give staff a map or dashboard backed by a reporting pipeline they can check against source records. When monthly totals differ between reports, staff need a way to trace the difference. Build the reconciliation step into the reporting process so staff can tell which records changed. Choose one number that staff already report. Trace it to the records, filters and calculation behind it. Try the service ledger demonstration . Select a district to compare its service records and hours. The CSV download follows the active district filter. Record how to treat a missing value, a correction and a row that was already present in the last refresh. Keep a small sample with known totals. A maintainer can run it again after a source field or reporting rule changes. For a map, preserve an identifier that lets a reviewer go from a point on the screen to the underlying record. 1. Source inventory Document the owner, format, refresh interval and allowed use of each source. Agree on a definition for each measure. Note when the source was last refreshed and which reporting period it covers. 2. Data preparation Validate incoming records, isolate exceptions and keep stable identifiers across refreshes. Include sample duplicates and missing values when checking the import. 3. Maps and reporting Design filters around decisions, include documented calculations and export the selected records. For an AI-assisted task, test its answers against a labeled sample before release. Open the export and reproduce the total using only its rows. 4. Scope and acceptance Filter a known sample, compare the count and sum to an independent calculation, then export the records and reproduce both numbers. Source quality, update frequency, geographic coverage, access rules and the number of reporting views drive effort. Open the planning guide · Scope and pricing

title: Mapping Indonesia’s industrial parks
description: How Rishabh Sinha built a public map and a repeatable publishing process for the University of Maryland’s Center for Global Sustainability.
keywords: Founder case study University of Maryland Morowali, Central Sulawesi Indonesia · July 2023 Center for Global Sustainability Mapping Indonesia’s industrial parks Overview The research team had a spreadsheet full of evidence about Indonesia’s industrial parks. Rishabh Sinha built the website that lets readers explore it, then gave the team a way to publish the next edition. Organization Center for Global Sustainability Role Research assistant · Website engineering Period Fall 2023 to spring 2025 Photograph of Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park in Central Sulawesi, July 2023. Ministry of Public Works of Indonesia . Explore the map Engineering Outcome Sources Industrial parks atlas · May 2025 Explore the archipelago. Shaded relief uses NASA Blue Marble ↗ . Rivers, boundaries and places come from Natural Earth ↗ . Select a numbered group to see its parks. From spreadsheet to public map An operating park might draw power from the national grid, from a captive coal plant or from both. Readers needed to switch from park status to electricity supply without losing their place on the map. When researchers corrected a record, the downloadable file needed to reflect the same change. A repeatable update Rishabh wrote a Python script that groups the master CSV fields into seven geographic files. He updated the public CSV download to use the master file and connected the site to the team’s selected ArcGIS map. A maintainer could regenerate the files, update the hosted layers and check the published map against the download. title: Evaluating an AI system
description: Rishabh authored a study on measuring whether a monitor can distinguish exposure to an instruction from a subsequent action.
keywords: AI monitor evaluation Research paper Return to top AI monitor evaluation Read paper Testing what an AI monitor can tell Rishabh authored a study on measuring whether a monitor can distinguish exposure to an instruction from a subsequent action. Read the paper and methods What the comparison found On the primary Qwen experiment, the monitor scored 0.853 AUROC and a trained text baseline scored 0.855. The paper shows how changing which examples enter the test changes what that score tells a reviewer. The study compares evaluation populations, reports results across models and includes a text baseline. The public paper links the experiment code. Relevance to a project For a buyer testing an assistant, the choice of examples matters. Evaluate correct answers, plausible errors and cases that should go to a human as separate groups.
